title: India Cuts Visa Categories From 13 to Nine, Renames Tourist Visa as Visitor Visa
excerpt: Sub-categories fall from 49 to 23 and application forms are to lose about 70% of their fields under the Home Ministry's Visa Manual review.
body:
• India will consolidate its 13 main visa categories into nine and cut sub-categories from 49 to 23, under a Union Home Ministry review of the Visa Manual, 2019.
  • The Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa (V), split into V-1 for short visits and V-2 for longer stays.
  • Application form fields are to be cut by about 70% by removing overlapping and repetitive questions.
  • The full list of the nine categories and a complete implementation timeline have not yet been published, so applicants should keep using the current categories until the new structure is notified.

India is simplifying the visa regime that foreign visitors, including the diaspora's relatives, spouses and friends, use to enter the country. The Union Home Ministry's review of the Visa Manual, 2019 will consolidate 13 main visa categories into nine, reduce sub-categories from 49 to 23, and rename the Tourist Visa as the Visitor Visa, according to The Hindu's reporting, summarised by Travelobiz.

What changes for visitors

The renamed Visitor Visa (V) has two sub-categories. V-1, for short-duration visits, covers tourism and sightseeing, visiting friends or relatives, business meetings and other short-term business activity, medical consultations and short-term treatment, wellness retreats and short yoga programmes, short courses in languages, music, dance and cooking, and transit-related travel. V-2 covers longer-duration visits for the activities previously permitted under the T-1 Tourist Visa, along with mountaineering expeditions. A September 2026 amendment also introduced an e-Group Visit Visa for foreign tourists arriving in India on cruise ships on a fixed itinerary.

For diaspora families, the practical effect is at the application stage rather than at the border: a relative who once had to choose between overlapping tourist, business and medical categories would apply under one Visitor Visa with a short- or long-duration sub-category. Eligibility and security checks are not being relaxed; what is being removed is duplication between categories.

The forms get much shorter

The second half of the overhaul is the paperwork. The government plans to remove approximately 70% of existing visa form fields by eliminating overlapping, repetitive and redundant questions, and the revised forms are expected to apply across visa categories. Earlier Hindu reporting on the same exercise said the current e-visa application runs to nine pages and that officials expected the simpler forms to arrive from next year; the e-visa itself, preceded by an electronic travel authorisation, is offered under nine sub-categories to nationals of 147 countries. Applications continue through the official Indian e-Visa portal in the meantime.

What is not yet known

Two decision-critical details are still missing. The Home Ministry has confirmed the reduction to nine main categories, but the final names and descriptions of all nine have not been made public, and the latest announcement does not give a complete implementation timeline. The rationalisation follows a meeting in August at which officials discussed amendments to chapters and appendices of the Visa Manual, 2019. Until the consolidated list is notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs, travellers should apply under the existing categories and should not assume the Visitor Visa label is live on application forms yet.

Why India is doing this

The stated aim of the review is to remove overlapping classifications and repetitive questions that burden applicants, and to bring the forms closer to global standards. For the diaspora, the audience most affected is not OCI cardholders, who do not need a visa, but the people around them: foreign-national spouses, in-laws, friends and colleagues travelling to India for weddings, family visits, medical care and tourism, for whom the nine-page form and the category maze have been the first friction point of the trip.
